dateline: Bamako / Kidal / Goubré / Tadjmart / Djibo / Diapaga — 2012–Present
heroHeadline: Day 27: Bamako Siege Holds; JNIM Expands into ISGS-Held Tillabéri; Eid Truce Window Closing; WFP/IRC Emergency Active
heroSubtitle: Day 27 of JNIM's declared 'total siege' of Bamako (announced April 28, 2026) continues with no resolution on any front as of May 25, 2026. The US Embassy in Bamako's Enhanced Security Alert (issued May 19) remains active through May 31, warning of route closures, fortified positions, and airport access threats. Three key developments define the current period: (1) JNIM TILLABÉRI INCURSION (May 22): JNIM claimed an attack in Niger's Tillabéri Region — historically IS-Sahel Province (ISSP) territory — signaling a deepening of the inter-jihadist territorial rivalry that erupted into direct armed clashes in April 2026 (50+ fighters killed on both sides). JNIM's expansion into ISGS turf in western Niger adds a new front to the multi-country simultaneous operations arc spanning Benin (Porga, May 7), Burkina Faso (Djibo May 11, Diapaga May 13, Goubré May 22), Mali (Bamako siege, Kidal aerial campaign), and Niger (Ménaka standoff, Tillabéri). (2) HUMANITARIAN EMERGENCY (Day 27): WFP remains suspended across the Central Sahel ($620M gap, 2M affected). IRC emergency response active in Mali. FAO's Cadre Harmonisé projects 52.8 million at acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3+) during June–August 2026 — the highest-ever Sahel lean-season projection — directly exacerbated by JNIM's sustained multi-country blockade operations. Bamako food prices remain +43–65% above pre-siege baselines; Manantali power grid degraded. (3) EID TRUCE WINDOW CLOSING: The March 2026 fuel-corridor deal (Mali released 100+ JNIM detainees; JNIM opened fuel supplies to Bamako) was nominally valid until approximately Eid al-Adha (late May–June 2026). The approaching Eid date adds structural uncertainty to Bamako's supply security beyond May 31. INTERNATIONAL ACCOUNTABILITY: The FIDH/TRIAL International/PALU African Court case (filed April 20) proceeds as the Goubré IDP camp massacre (80 killed May 22) and Africa Corps cluster bomb allegations (Tadjmart, May 16–17) generate sustained IHL documentation. No ceasefire negotiations reported as of May 25, 2026.
